title: The Long-Horizon SOTA Is a Harness, Not a Model
summary: Ramain configurations define the long-horizon cost-performance frontier, from near-frontier results at $0.16 to the highest score in the evaluation.
body_markdown:
## Every point on the frontier is a Ramain configuration


We tested Ramain, Claude Code, and Codex on the same long-horizon enterprise browser tasks. On GPT-6 Astra, Ramain reached 89.4% success at $1.04 per task, against Codex at 88.2% and $2.55. On Fable 5.1, Ramain reached 88.2% at $0.79, against Claude Code at 87.1% and $1.38.


The cheapest configuration shows how far the harness carries a small model. Ramain on Gemini 3.8 Flash reached 85.9% success at $0.16 per task, within 1.2 points of Claude Code on Fable 5.1 at nearly nine times lower cost, and within 2.3 points of Codex on GPT-6 Astra at sixteen times lower cost.


With the same Gemini 3.8 Flash model, Ramain used 37,000 context tokens per task on average versus 165,000 for Codex. Ramain achieved higher performance while costing four times less.


Ramain configurations define the cost-performance frontier across Gemini 3.8 Flash, Fable 5.1, and GPT-6 Astra.
